title: Inguinal hernia and undescended testis in an infant

header.contentArea: Paediatric surgery: groin and scrotum in infancy
guidelineVersions: RCS England/BAPS commissioning guide: paediatric orchidopexy (2015)

related.why: Testicular tumours, one reason undescended testes matter

brief.scenario: Leo Ramsden, a 6-week-old boy born at term, has a right groin swelling that appears when he cries and goes away when he settles. At his 6–8 week check the GP could not feel his right testis in the scrotum. His parents are with him.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the diagnosis and management of both problems.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Two problems, two clocks: the hernia needs repair soon; the testis needs surgery in the second half of the first year or soon after.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Waiting to see if an infant hernia closes, or treating it like an adult hernia.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "This sounds like a right indirect inguinal hernia and a right undescended testis. I'd examine both sides."

grid.label: Diagnosis and embryology
grid.fail: Calls it a direct hernia or a hydrocele without examining.
grid.pass: Right indirect inguinal hernia from a patent processus vaginalis; right undescended testis.
grid.high: Separates hernia from hydrocele: you cannot get above a hernia and it reduces; a hydrocele may transilluminate, but bowel in infants can too.

grid.label: Timing of hernia repair
grid.fail: Says infant hernias close on their own, so waits.
grid.pass: Lists for repair soon, ideally within two weeks, because infant hernias do not resolve and incarceration risk is highest in the first year.
grid.high: Cites that waiting over 14 days doubled incarceration in infants under 1; teaches parents the signs of incarceration.

grid.label: Incarceration
grid.fail: Sends home an irreducible hernia, or goes straight to theatre without attempting reduction in a well baby.
grid.pass: Analgesia and gentle taxis, admit, repair within days once swelling settles; emergency surgery if irreducible or signs of strangulation.
grid.high: Notes the testis can infarct from cord compression; ex-premature infants need postoperative apnoea monitoring.

grid.label: The operation
grid.pass: Herniotomy (open or laparoscopic): separate the sac from the vas and vessels, ligate it at the deep ring; no mesh, no posterior wall repair.
grid.high: Laparoscopy lets you see and close a contralateral patent processus; handle the vas gently.

grid.label: Timing of orchidopexy
grid.fail: Plans review at school age, or promises it will come down.
grid.pass: Knows most descend in the first months of life; refers early and plans orchidopexy in infancy, not at school age.
grid.high: EAU: operate before 12 months, by 18 months at the latest. UK guide: ultrasound not indicated; bilateral undescended needs early endocrine assessment.

grid.label: Impalpable testis
grid.fail: Orders an ultrasound to find it.
grid.pass: Examination under anaesthesia and diagnostic laparoscopy at a tertiary centre; ultrasound cannot reliably find or exclude an abdominal testis.
grid.high: Bilateral impalpable testes in a newborn: urgent assessment for a difference of sex development, such as congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

grid.label: Counselling
grid.fail: Tells parents orchidopexy removes the cancer risk.
grid.pass: Explains why: fertility, cancer risk, easier examination; risks: atrophy, reascent, vas or vessel injury; day-case surgery.
grid.high: Quotes relative cancer risk 2.2 with orchidopexy before 13 versus 5.4 after, and advises testicular self-examination later.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: It reduces and has a cough impulse on crying. When would you repair it?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: They often close by themselves, so I'd see him at a year.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: He comes in with an irreducible, tender lump. He's well otherwise.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd take him straight to theatre.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd review him when he starts school.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: His parents ask if surgery removes the cancer risk.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes, once it's down he's normal.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A right indirect inguinal hernia through a patent processus vaginalis, and a right undescended testis.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: When would you repair the hernia?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Soon, ideally within two weeks. Infant hernias don't close and incarceration is most likely in the first year.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: He comes in with an irreducible lump.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Analgesia and gentle taxis, admit, then repair within a few days once the swelling settles. If it won't reduce or there's strangulation, emergency surgery.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Herniotomy: separate the sac from the vas and vessels and ligate it at the deep ring. No mesh, no posterior wall repair.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: 3 to 5% are undescended at term and most come down by 3 months. He should be seen by 6 months, with orchidopexy at 6 to 18 months.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Examination under anaesthesia and laparoscopy at a tertiary centre. Ultrasound can't reliably find it.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What would you tell his parents?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It's for fertility, lower cancer risk and easier examination. Risks are atrophy, reascent and vas injury. Usually a day case.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How would you tell it from a hydrocele?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: You can't get above a hernia and it reduces. Transillumination doesn't help much, because infant bowel can transilluminate too.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: In one large series, infants under 1 who waited more than 14 days had double the incarceration risk. I'd teach his parents the warning signs: a hard, tender lump, vomiting, or an unsettled baby.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The testis can infarct from pressure on the cord. If he'd been premature, he'd need apnoea monitoring after the anaesthetic.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Either. Laparoscopy lets me see and close a patent processus on the other side.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What does European guidance say about timing?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Before 12 months, and by 18 months at the latest; ultrasound doesn't help. UK guidance adds that if both were undescended, he'd need early endocrine assessment.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: And a newborn with both testes impalpable?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Urgent assessment for a difference of sex development, such as congenital adrenal hyperplasia, before anything else.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Does surgery remove the cancer risk?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No. It lowers it: relative risk about 2.2 with orchidopexy before 13, against 5.4 after. He should learn self-examination as a teenager.

failures.move: Waiting for an infant hernia to close.
failures.consequence: Incarceration, with risk to bowel and testis.
The problem is a patent sac, not a weak wall; herniotomy is the operation.

failures.move: Deferring the testis to school age.
failures.consequence: Germ cell loss continues; later fertility is worse.

failures.move: Relying on ultrasound for an impalpable testis.
failures.consequence: Cannot exclude an abdominal testis; laparoscopy is still needed.

recovery.when: Asked why infant hernias differ from adult ones
recovery.line: It's a patent processus vaginalis, so the fix is to tie off the sac, not repair the wall.
Hernia within weeks; testis seen by 6 months and fixed by 18 months.

knowledge.fact: Waiting over 14 days doubled incarceration risk in infants under 1 year awaiting repair.
Undescended testis: 3–5% at term; most descend by 3 months; no spontaneous descent after that.
UK: see by 6 months; orchidopexy 6–18 months; ultrasound not indicated; impalpable testis needs laparoscopy; bilateral needs early endocrine assessment.
EAU: orchidopexy before 12 months, by 18 months at latest. Cancer relative risk 2.2 if operated before 13, 5.4 after.

recall.think: Incarcerated hernia threatens bowel and testis; a late orchidopexy costs fertility.
recall.say: "Right indirect inguinal hernia: list for herniotomy soon. Right undescended testis: orchidopexy at 6 to 18 months."
do: List hernia repair within two weeks

numbers.meaning: wait beyond which incarceration risk doubles in infants

recall.trap: Infant hernias do not close on their own, and orchidopexy lowers but does not remove the cancer risk.
recall.finish: Herniotomy now; orchidopexy at 6–18 months, or laparoscopy if impalpable.

sources.supports: Orchidopexy before 12 months and by 18 months at the latest; ultrasound lacks sensitivity; EUA and laparoscopy for impalpable testis; relative risk of testicular cancer 2.2 before age 13 and 5.4 after

partner.opening: Leo's parents have brought him to clinic. What do you think the swelling is?

reveals.finding: Right groin swelling extending towards the scrotum on crying; reduces easily; cannot get above it.
Left testis in the scrotum. Right testis palpable in the groin; cannot be brought into the scrotum.

push.question: What is the swelling, and why has it happened?
push.expect: Indirect hernia via patent processus vaginalis.

push.question: He returns with an irreducible lump. What now?
push.expect: Analgesia, taxis, admit, repair in days; theatre if irreducible or strangulated.

push.question: Describe the operation.
push.expect: Herniotomy at the deep ring; no mesh.

push.question: When should the testis be fixed?
What will you tell the parents?
push.expect: Reasons, risks, cancer risk reduced not removed.

curveballs.safeAnswer: A peritoneal pouch that precedes the testis through the inguinal canal; if it stays open it causes an indirect hernia or hydrocele.

curveballs.prompt: Should he have an ultrasound to find the testis?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No: it is palpable, and ultrasound is not indicated; an impalpable testis needs laparoscopy.
Plan repair before discharge or soon after, with postoperative apnoea monitoring.

curveballs.prompt: Will orchidopexy stop him getting testicular cancer?
curveballs.safeAnswer: It lowers the risk but does not remove it; self-examination later.
